torch.geqrf spends 79% in the relaunched, memory-bound geqr2 panel kernel. Write a custom Triton blocked-Householder QR, one CTA per matrix: factor a width-b column panel kept resident in shared memory (sequential reflector loop), form the T factor, then apply the block reflector to the trailing submatrix via tl.dot. Fuse panel+trailing-update to eliminate the thousands of tiny per-step relaunches. Target the batched n=512 cluster (4 of 12 shapes). Emit packed (H,tau); FP32 reflectors; pass all ill-conditioned guards. Tune b in {16,32,64}.

Blocked Householder QR (compact-WY) in Triton for n=512: 3 batched kernels/panel (one-CTA panel factor + larft T, atomic compute_S, parallel apply). ieee dots (TF32 broke factor gate). Off-grid n -> geqrf. n=512 964ms->139ms. All tests+guards PASS.

Fuse trailing update into one col-tile kernel: per-program S=V^T@A_tile via row-subtile reduction (no atomics/scratch/zeroing), then A_tile-=V@(T^T@S). Eliminates atomic kernel, scratch buf, zero_, double A-read. RT=64 CT=64. n=512 964ms->12.2ms (79x). Geomean 26794us (4.32x). All tests+guards PASS.

L2 cache-blocking: process batch in chunks of 160 matrices through all panels (working set ~160MB ~ 134MB L2), turning the HBM-bound trailing kernel's repeated per-panel reads into L2 hits. Swept chunk {32..640}; 160 (4 even chunks of 640) is the sweet spot vs SM starvation. n=512 12.2ms->10.5ms. Geomean 25577us (4.53x). Tests+guards PASS.

Brief-0 exhausted. Best: commit 409fb0e5, geomean 25576.572us = 4.53x baseline (115780us); n=512 batch=640 shapes 964ms->10.5ms (~91x). Built a Triton blocked-Householder (compact-WY) QR for n=512: (1) one-CTA-per-matrix panel factor (sequential reflector loop, panel resident in smem, forms BxB T factor); (2) fused single-kernel trailing update A_trail-=V@(T^T@(V^T@A)) over (batch,col_tile) grid with row-subtile reduction (no atomics/scratch); (3) L2 cache-blocking CHUNK=160 (the non-obvious win, +4.5% geomean: batch chunked through all panels so trailing reads hit the 134MB L2 not HBM). Off-grid n -> geqrf (offgrid guard clean). All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. KEY FP32 finding: tl.dot MUST be input_precision=ieee; plain tf32 hits scaled-factor-residual 27.5 (>20 gate, fails on clustered/ill-cond). EXHAUSTED knobs: B{8,16,32}->32 best, RT/CT 64/64 best, num_warps/stages 8/4/2 best, CHUNK 160 best, tf32x3 slower than ieee, T-build split & alpha/xnorm2 reduction-fusion no win, two-level/super-panel blocking SLOWER (build_T extra pass + wider tiles drop occupancy). BOTTLENECK (ncu): panel-factor ~5.7ms is latency/update-bound, occupancy capped at 1 block/SM by the 64KB smem panel tile (B=32) AND 220 regs/thread; trailing ~5.0ms is L2/HBM-bound (was 80% DRAM, cache-blocking relieved it). SUGGESTED NEXT (need fresh brief / outside n=512 lane): (a) the geomean is now dominated by the 3 n=1024 shapes (~220ms each, still geqrf) and n=2048/4096 - biggest remaining lever is a custom path there (other workers' lane); (b) for n=512 a further win likely needs a fundamentally more-parallel panel factorization that doesn't pin one 64KB-smem CTA per matrix (e.g. warp-specialized or a smem-light panel) to lift the 16% occupancy ceiling; (c) worker-2's reduced-precision trailing (tf32 with re-orthogonalization) could be combined with my structure since plain tf32 is faster but needs the orthogonality recovered.

Break the panel-factor 16%-occupancy ceiling (1 block/SM, capped by the 64KB resident [n,B] smem tile + 220 regs/thread) -- it bottlenecks BOTH n=512 and n=1024 (7 of 12 shapes), so a win compounds. Replace the one-CTA-per-matrix sequential panel with a TSQR / communication-avoiding factorization: split each matrix's tall panel into row-blocks factored by SEPARATE CTAs (far more CTAs -> fills all 188 SMs, each block's smem is small/non-resident), then merge the R-blocks (binary-tree or single combiner). CRITICAL RISK to retire first: emitting a single geqrf-compatible packed (H,tau) from tree-merged reflectors is fragile -- mitigate by computing R via TSQR then doing ONE re-factor pass of the panel against the final R to produce canonical reflectors, rather than merging tree reflectors directly. Keep the existing multi-CTA col-tile trailing update and CHUNK L2-blocking. Packed (H,tau) FP32, geqrf-grade accuracy; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress any shape.

Restore L2 cache-blocking (per-n CHUNK) dropped in the n=1024 merge: n=512 CHUNK=160 (4x160 of batch=640, ~160MB L2-resident) 12.2->10.9ms; n=1024 CHUNK huge (60-CTA grid already underfilled, chunking starves it, swept 16..60). Geomean 11593us (9.99x). Tests+guards PASS.

Brief-1 done. WIN: commit 52cd7e1c, geomean 11593us = 9.99x (from parent 9.73x/11893us) by RESTORING my L2 cache-blocking that the n=1024 merge dropped (n=512 CHUNK=160: 12.2->10.9ms; n=1024 keep CHUNK huge -- its 60-CTA grid is already underfilled so chunking starves it, swept 16..60). All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. TSQR = DEAD END (real attempt, hard evidence): the brief's mechanism (TSQR-R + re-factor-against-R for canonical reflectors) is NUMERICALLY VALID -- I proved the Householder reconstruction tau_j*v_j = e_j - (H_1..H_{j-1})Q[:,j] with Q=A R^-1 reproduces geqrf packed (H,tau) to FP64 machine precision. BUT it does NOT break the occupancy ceiling: I built the reconstruction kernel and ncu shows it has the IDENTICAL bottleneck to the original factor -- 255 regs/thread, Block-Limit-Registers=1, Block-Limit-Smem=1, 16.6% occupancy, 174us/panel (vs original 172us) -- because emitting CANONICAL packed reflectors forces the same sequential per-column generation with the tall [n,B] panel resident. TSQR only parallelizes R (480 CTAs for n=1024), but R was NEVER the bottleneck; the sequential reflector/reconstruction with the resident panel is, and that is IRREDUCIBLE under the geqrf-packed-output contract. The full TSQR pipeline (TSQR-R + Q=AR^-1 + merge + reconstruction) does strictly MORE work than the single current factor (174us reconstruction alone ~ 172us full factor, before adding 3 phases) and FP32 reconstruction accuracy is marginal (V err 5.6e-3). Also confirmed n=1024 nw_pf=8/VT=128 already optimal (16 warps slower). CONCLUSION: the panel-factor occupancy ceiling cannot be broken by row-block parallelism while the output must be canonical packed (H,tau). SUGGESTED NEXT: (a) the geomean is now dominated by the geqrf shapes n=2048(74ms)/n=4096(50ms)/n=352(38ms)/n=176(15ms) -- biggest lever is custom paths there; (b) for n=512/1024 the only remaining angle is reduced-precision (worker-2 lane: tf32 trailing + re-orthogonalize) which is orthogonal to occupancy; (c) accept the panel factor as-is -- it is at the canonical-output speed-of-light for one-CTA-per-matrix.

You proved TSQR can't break the panel occupancy ceiling (irreducible under packed-(H,tau)) -- so pivot to the ORTHOGONAL lever you measured: tf32 tensor-core trailing is ~5% faster at n=512 but fails the factor gate (scaled residual 27.5>20) on clustered/ill-conditioned inputs UNCORRECTED. Make it SAFE for n=512/1024: run the larfb-style trailing update V*(T^T*(V^T*A)) in tf32 (or bf16) tensor cores with FP32 accumulate, then recover accuracy via a correction -- e.g. one step of iterative refinement on the trailing residual, or compute the trailing update in tf32 then add an fp32 low-rank correction for the dropped mantissa bits. Panel factorization + reflectors + tau stay exact FP32. Target: capture the ~5% trailing speedup on n=512/1024 (7 of 12 shapes) while passing the clustered/rankdef/band factor gate (20*n*eps) and the 100*n*eps orthogonality gate. If correction costs more than the tf32 saving, that's a valid negative finding. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress.

[NEGATIVE] tf32x3 trailing GEMM for n=512/1024 (only gate-safe reduced-precision variant). Validates PASS (all gates incl clustered/rankdef) but geomean 6915->7104us, a 2.7% REGRESSION (n512 12.5->13.2ms, n1024 8.7->9.0ms). Root cause (ncu): trailing kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound (74.7% DRAM, 36% compute), so reduced-precision GEMM gives no speedup and tf32x3's 3 tc passes are slower than ieee 1 SIMT pass. Reverting to parent.

Brief-2 = NEGATIVE FINDING (real attempt, validated end-to-end). Reduced-precision tensor-core trailing CANNOT net-win for n=512/1024 on the global best; parent 6266257b (geomean 6915us here) stays best. EVIDENCE: (1) The trailing kernel is MEMORY-BANDWIDTH-BOUND -- ncu: 74.7% DRAM, 36% compute SM. So reduced-precision GEMM math gives ZERO speedup: the FP32 data load/store dominates regardless of multiply precision (the brief scopes 'only the GEMM' reduced-precision, storage stays FP32, so traffic is unchanged). (2) End-to-end on the parent (HBM-bound), plain tf32 is actually SLOWER than ieee (n512 12.62 vs 12.25ms) AND fails the gate (scaled-factor-residual 47.6/24.1 > 20 on clustered/n512,n1024). (3) tf32x3 (the ONLY gate-safe variant: 3-term error-compensated, validates PASS on all 22 tests + 3 guards incl clustered/rankdef/band) REGRESSES geomean 6915->7104us (-2.7%, committed d3dc4eb7, reverted): its 3 tensor-core passes + conversion cost more than ieee's 1 SIMT pass on a memory-bound kernel. (4) Cheaper corrections don't thread the needle: I prototyped 2-term split-GEMM (split only the dynamic-range operand A) -> rel err 1.0e-3 vs tf32 1.8e-3 vs ieee 2.2e-7 => would still give scaled-residual ~26 > 20 (V truncation dominates; you must split BOTH operands = 3 terms = tf32x3 = no win). Iterative refinement adds a 2nd pass on a memory-bound kernel = strictly slower. (5) The ~7% tf32 speedup I saw in brief-0 only exists in the CACHE-BLOCKED (L2-bound) regime (cb-ieee 10.92 vs cb-tf32 10.13ms), but even there tf32x3 is break-even (10.86ms) and no safe correction captures it. CONCLUSION: precision is the wrong lever -- the trailing update is bandwidth-bound; the win would have to come from REDUCING MEMORY TRAFFIC (lower-precision STORAGE of the trailing working set), which is out of this brief's scope (FP32 storage / GEMM-only) and is risky for accuracy. SUGGESTED NEXT: target the still-geqrf big shapes n=4096 (~50ms, 2 CTAs) and improving n=2048; or a storage-precision experiment (bf16 trailing buffer + FP32 master) as a separate brief if accuracy can be held.

Your single-kernel n=512/1024 levers are tapped (occupancy ceiling irreducible, trailing bandwidth-bound, precision dead) -- so attack UTILIZATION across kernels: both the panel-factor (~16% occ, compute/latency-bound) and the trailing (~16% occ, bandwidth-bound) leave ~84% of SMs idle, and different batch-CHUNKs are fully independent. Pipeline them with CUDA streams: process chunk B's panel-factor concurrently with chunk A's trailing (offset by one phase) so the occupancy-bound panel overlaps the bandwidth-bound trailing and fills idle SMs. Target n=512 (batch640, 4 chunks) primarily, n=1024 if it helps. CRITICAL tension to measure: 2 concurrent chunks ~double the L2 working set and may break the CHUNK=160 L2-residency win -- sweep chunk size / stream count to find the overlap-vs-L2 sweet spot. If stream overlap can't beat the serial CHUNK baseline, that's a valid negative finding. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress n=1024/2048/352/4096.

Brief-3 = NEGATIVE FINDING (real attempt). Cross-kernel overlap is REAL but INACCESSIBLE under the constraints; parent 7a64cd7a stays best (no code change). EVIDENCE: (1) The overlap upside is real -- I measured (throwaway probe) that running 2 independent n=512 chunks' panel+trailing CONCURRENTLY on two CUDA streams is 12.0% faster than serially (4.36 vs 4.96ms), confirming the occupancy-bound panel overlaps the bandwidth-bound trailing and fills idle SMs (panel 6.7% DRAM + trailing 74.7% DRAM = 81% fits; compute 41%+36%=77% fits). (2) BUT CUDA STREAMS ARE HARD-BANNED: harness/validate.sh has a banned-construct scan (case-insensitive substring 'stream' -> exit 3 validation_error) because the GPU MODE leaderboard DISQUALIFIES any submission doing work on another stream ('This is not allowed and may result in your disqualification'). So torch.cuda.Stream is forbidden both locally AND remotely; evading the substring check would be reward-hacking AND still DQ remotely. (3) The ONLY stream-free concurrency mechanism is a fused heterogeneous-grid MEGAKERNEL (one launch, programs split by pid into panel-role + trailing-role). I built and measured it: it is 3.7% SLOWER than the serial two-kernel phase (0.243 vs 0.234ms). Triton compiles ONE kernel with the UNION of both roles' resources (panel needs 64KB resident smem + trailing tiles), so BOTH roles run at the worse (1 block/SM) occupancy and the pid-branch divergence wastes SIMT lanes -- the megakernel cannot preserve the per-kernel occupancy that made the 2-stream version win. A persistent work-queue megakernel hits the same union-resource wall. CONCLUSION: the cross-kernel utilization lever exists (12% on n=512) but is unreachable -- streams are banned/DQ, and the stream-free megakernel defeats itself via the occupancy union. This closes the utilization branch. SUGGESTED NEXT: pivot off n=512/1024 entirely (all my levers there -- occupancy/TSQR, precision, overlap -- are now exhausted/blocked). Biggest remaining geomean lever is the still-on-geqrf n=4096 (~50ms, batch=2: needs multi-CTA-per-matrix since the fused path's 2-CTA grid was 25x slower) and squeezing n=2048; or a simplify pass on the combined best.
